content: Mortis A time for love, a time for hate, a time for peace ,  and a time for war. - Book of Aurtus "It is not like him to make someone of your stature wait, Lord Speaker," the older woman stated, gracefully making her way across the large marble study. The staccato sound of her wooden shoes echoing off the cavernous stone walls caused Darius to wince at each click of the oak heel against the virgin white stone.  The old woman caught the reaction, a small smile adorning her face as she came to stand before him. Despite her advanced age, her movements were sure and steady—that of someone much younger. Darius stood stalwart; the only movement was his eyes, tracking her form with feigned disinterest. With a smile, she moved again, disappearing beyond even his peripheral vision.  Darius quickly felt the uncomfortable heat of her stare on the back of his neck, and he turned to face her, realizing too late that she had forced him to move.  She has bested me,  he thought, wincing internally.  So, it is to be power games.   The woman's steel grey demeanor lent to her disposition as well as her coloring . T hirty years  prior , she would have been able to easily get by with her looks  but to be in the  king 's inner circle at her age, she must have been more than a beautiful face. This was a woman of the court, a woman whose job it was to understand him. She was the  king 's advanced team. And she was someone to be reckoned with.  Darius met her eyes, taking in the harsh but pleasant features of her face as she continued to observe him quietly. He suppressed a shiver. Her gaze was predatory, like looking into the dead, black eyes of a shark. She was calculated and deliberate, every movement, motion, and position purposely thought out. Like a game of chess, her every goal was eliciting reactions, assessing them, looking for weaknesses. Darius knew this game well and how to play.   He was no stranger to the games of royalty; in his time as a speaker, he had come head to head with princes and kings. This woman would not best him. Darius turned to face  her , keeping his back straight and shoulders squared, giving the impression of strength. Despite being taken by force from his sanctuary, he refused to show fear or confusion. Quietly he continued to track the woman as she half-turned gracefully, gliding to the old mahogany standing bar in the corner of the study. With expert movements, she plucked a glass from under the counter and poured something dark into a crystal snifter. The woman motioned with the cut-glass decanter towards Darius and waited a moment. With a shake of his head, he refused the proffered drink. The woman shrugged, a small smile spreading over her face as she topped off her glass, and then, in one swift motion, brought the tumbler to her lips and downed the amber liquid in a single gulp. She  slightly bowed to the Lord Speaker.  And I pass another test , Darius thought, bending at the waist to return the respectful gesture. Darius lowered his cowl, fully revealing his striking features. Not an uncommon reaction, her eyes widened at the sight. His bright blue eyes stood out against his dark Mediterranean skin and black hair. The  speaker  knew his features were a rarity in this region, a gift from his long-deceased mother.  In  this land of alabaster skin and blonde hair,  it was  rare and very noticeable. Darius took a calming breath, getting control of the indignance that had shadowed his mood since being whisked away to this place.  He had remained alone in this study for the entire day and had fallen back on his training. So here he had stood, except for a single investigative tour of the room, focusing on every detail available , u sing the time to take in every clue. Since entering the study under escort from the royal guard that morning, he had collected quite a bit of information.  The  speaker  knew the simple meditative state was unsettling for others to see; they would quickly grow uncomfortable. They had always felt the need to fill the silent space with movement and sound.  That discomfort had, more than once, proved to be an advantage for him.   Darius smiled as he recalled how well it had worked over the years, one of the first lessons learned as a child when upon the path of Speaker. He  studied the woman's expensive blue silk gown and handmade ,  white shoes. She is a woman of means, someone who ha d  had to adapt within a court of men. To hold a position of power like this, she had to be better by far than any man. The deep lines of her aged face spoke of skill and competence   and  told of shrewd experience. But Darius  recognized her easygoing smile and relaxed demeanor as the mask it truly was.  "It is fine. I am sure the  king  has much to do," Darius responded, speaking for the first time , his  almost melodic voice  selling the  forced pleasantry. Darius would keep his ego in check and not allow the actions of this impertinent  king  to dictate his response. The  king  had overstepped his authority, but he didn't need to point that out, didn't need to yell and threaten. No, this man would not have done such a thing without reason.  Understand, empathize, and visualize the motive,  he told himself, again relying on the priests' teaching s . "Do you know why I was summoned this day?" he asked, his tone still easy as he tried to pry what information he could from her. Her body language quickly chang ed , becoming stiff as she merely shook her head. The practiced smile faltering for only a moment.  She knows,  he thought.  She knows and was ordered to be silent. Soldiers had removed Darius from the  K eep, from his very sanctuary . A nger flash ed  through his mind at the thought. Those actions alone would be enough to anger the Church elders. Or worse. This  king  threatened the peace that had spilled so much innocent blood only  five   centuries   previous.   To break that peace would mean a world bathed again in blood. Darius remember ed  the history lessons of the Blood King's reign and the Mage Wars. He shivered, recalling reading of the brutal battles and slaughter and torture of innocents, all in the name of purity. His eyes shifted away from the old woman to the rows and rows of books along the walls. The collection was  well used, so if this was indeed the  king 's study, then the man was incredibly well-read.  "Speaker Darius," the woman spoke with carefully measured words, "your escort here was not decided lightly, and the  king  is well aware he tempts fate with his actions. But I assure you once you hear what he has to say, you will understand. I will tell you this is probably the most important case you have ever taken." The  king  knew a speaker's position was beyond the authority of this world. No one dared to interfere with a speaker performing the duties of his office. He answered to no man, no mortal law, and certainly, no king, the man's audacity knew no bounds, and the thought added to Darius's anger.  "I apologize for keeping you waiting," came the friendly  baritone   from the door, startling the two from their silent contemplation.  Darius caught the woman's penitent genuflection out of the corner of his eye.  This must be   King Alaric . He forced a smile ,  making  a dismissive motion for the woman to stand  and  turning his attention to Darius at once.   The smile never leaving his face, he waited for only a moment for him to bow as well.  Darius did not. The  king  moved on, making no mention nor showing any displeasure at the spurn. The woman eyed Darius  as she approached the  k ing , and out of his peripheral vision, he could make out the disapproval playing across her face.  She  paused  at his side  to exchange a meaningful glance and a few soft words.  He  nodd ed  as she passed him ,  and  she left the room . King Alaric stepped quickly towards the  modest gathering of furniture at the  center of the study. With a  practiced ,  theatrical flourish, he swept his long, green gown out of the way and settled into a deep leather chair. Alaric's smile stood sentry against the tsunami of emotion he was  obviously  holding  back;  his tired eyes studied the  speaker .  Interesting , Darius thought  he truly feels the weight of his son's loss . Without even a by your leave, Darius took control of the moment, taking a step forward to speak. "Your Majesty, your actions flaunt authority you do not have. Please tell me you do not tempt the breaking of the peace that has lasted so long, simply because your son was killed.  "I understand this will shake your rule as it leaves ascension to the throne  uncertain ,  but  listening to an advisor who would tell you to kidnap a speaker, despite your reservations, is near madness." Darius allowed a hint of the annoyance he had been suppressing all day to color his tone. The man's smile never left his face; however, his head shifted slightly to the side. "She has told you much. I am surprised. But you're right; it was her idea—and a daring one at that." Darius wav ed  off the comment, pacing the study. "Rest easy, King, she did not divulge anything. I am a speaker. This is what we do." He pointed to the shelves. "The library is vast. The layer of dust near the lip of the shelves is evident, except for in front of one book…the book of succession,  w hich means someone has been looking into who succeeds the throne should you or your son die." "The vials on the table smell of almonds, which means it's cyanide. However, the y  were moved aside," Darius continued, sounding  like   an instructor scolding an impertinent student. "And slight indentations in the table show that someone has been copying runic script. From that,  I can conclude your son was not poisoned but allegedly killed with magic . "   The  king 's  eyes narrowed, shifting away from the  speaker  to study the tabletop, clearly trying to see what Darius had. He knew the  king  would not see the slight indentations a quill made in soft pine. It took years of training and command of magic to see it. Darius brought his lesson to a conclusion. "And finally, I caught the look between the two of you and heard her whisper 'give him a chance,' making the entire scenario obvious." Though finished having his say, Darius did not sit, did not yield, bent on proving the  king  was not the power in the room, for Darius was a servant of the Keep. He answered to one who was greater than even Alaric. The  king  studied Darius, the smile falling from his face as grief overtook  him . This  must have been   more than simple politics for Alaric. He truly grieved for the death of his son. He came to sit across from this grieving father, settling into an identical leather chair and pausing for a moment to forcibly quell his aggravation. The father's heart ached, and Darius offered what comfort he could, laying a gentle hand on the  king 's arm. The  king  nodded his thanks. "I know what I have done is a crime. Artus's ass, what I have done could undo the damned Agreement, but Lord Speaker, I don't care. I need to know who killed Banis. He was my world and has been since my wife was taken from me. Someone is playing a cruel game, Speaker, and I beg you to find out who." Alaric struggled to gather himself, his watery eyes holding back  the  tears as his voice shook. With an effort of  sheer will, he continued. "My son is dead. The light of my life. And he has been taken from me." The deluge finally broke free, streaming down Alaric's face, the torchlight reflecting against the river of sorrow along his face. Darius watched the man as he emotionally unraveled. Yes, this man had threatened to break the Agreement, the compact between Church, Mage, and Mundane, the pact that allowed all three to live in peace. Darius reflected as his hand went unconsciously to the brand on his cheek,  the   one that marked him as a mage, one of the concessions made to stop the killing of his people when the Agreement was signed. Alaric's voice  became   hard ,  the pain and grieving transforming to anger as his face grew cold and his eyes distant, breaking Darius from his thoughts as the  king  spoke. "He was killed to ensure I had no  heir,  I know it .  T here are those who wish to end my reign, to end the line of my family ruling this land . T hey mean to exterminate my bloodline, Speaker. This cannot—this  will not  happen," the  king  declared. Darius settled back into the chair, this was not the first time he had listened to a parent recall the death of their child, and though it was something he had done many times, he felt the man's pain , c ould see how it was eating him alive, as if a hole had suddenly appeared in his soul, eroding the substance that made him corporeal. If Alaric did not gain control of himself, hide this weakness, this pain, his court would descend upon him like a pack of hungry wolves, devouring the man even if he wasn't outright killed. The court would find a way to take control .  Alaric could find himself a puppet king; the  speaker  studied this man, this father, this  king . The logical tactician gave way to the man, no ,  the priest he realized with surprise, his heart went out to Alaric, not the  king , but for this grieving father . O n the outside, Darius remained stoic, allowing the  king  to take his time and tell the story. Alaric looked as if he had aged ten years in an instant as  he began to recall the story . "The servants found him yesterday, in his room, slumped over his table. The look on his face…th-the blood, it is as if he vomited every ounce within him.   The look on his face was one of pain, Speaker; someone had caused him so much pain, his muscles were twisted as if he were trying to claw off his skin."   As the last words echoed off the stone study, the only sound heard was the  king 's soft sobbing. After a time, Darius leaned forward. "I will speak for your son, my king," he whispered, watching as the other man's shoulders slumped with relief. With those words, Darius had absolved the  king  of his crime against himself and the Church.   By taking on this task, he had given his bond, his word, that Darius, Speaker of Aurtus, would now tell the story of this man's son. He would search out those responsible and bring their dark deed into the light; no man could stand in his way; no place was forbidden, for he was the bringer of truth. ***  Darius found himself being led by an old man dressed in well-polished light leather armor.   The soldier hobbled  forward ,  an injury on his right leg, causing a very pronounced limp .   H is position is one of honor. This  is  a man who  has  been rewarded for his service to the crown ,  Darius surmised,  as  he tried  and failed  to keep track of the ir  route . Having spent the day in the large warm study, Darius became keenly aware of the sun going down and the cold October evening settling into the old stone castle.   Pulling the thin grey robe around him, he did his best to battle the chilly air as the y traveled  through hall after hall, around corners, and down long flights of stairs. "The body is kept in the lower level to keep it cool," the gravelly voice of the old soldier announced as the two made their way down the third flight of stairs, descending once again for what seemed like an eternity. The torch carried by the old man quickly became the only light , but  Darius could see the change in the stone as they fell beneath the ground, the old stone becoming damp and moss-covered. The further they  went , the more treacherous the footing became. Darius felt his leather sandals giving way to the slick rock beneath his feet.  The  speaker  marveled at the elderly man's surety, descending at a good clip despite the limp and never losing his footing. Darius reached out and touched the dripping water as it caressed a newly formed stalactite. This section of the castle was slowly being taken back by the subterranean plants, the lush vines flourishing from cracks in the stone walls and flowing over the damp moss - ridden floor. Finally, the soldier stopped, pointing to a large wooden door. "I will go no further, Lord Speaker, but what you seek is within that room," he stated  with fear in his  eyes,  torchlight casting an eerie light on his thin white hair  and fissured skin. Turning towards the dark  entrance, the  soldier  made a quick furtive gesture with his hand. Darius  tried   to remember the name of the ancient, pagan religion and then smiled .   Catholicism. The man had made a cross in the air, and as he walked towards the light at the end of the hall,  he   softly chanted  in an ancient language, "Hail Mary, full of grace…". People still practiced that dark religion , he mused, moving away from the soldier, the chant diminishing behind him.  As Darius reached for the door’s handle, he was surprised as  it swung open, revealing a squat, fat man with a contagious grin and intelligent eyes. "Hello, Lord Speaker," the rotund man began excitedly, his bald head covered in sweat despite the chill in the air. " I t is quite the honor to meet one such as you . P lease, please come in . "  He  took the  small, stained  cloth to his shiny dome, moving to the side  to allow  Darius to enter. The  speaker  cautiously entered the small room,  grimacing  at the stench of decay that hung heavy in the air.  P ushing out with his will ,  Darius whispered ,  " N on nidore," his blue eyes flashing white as he infused the words with his  magical power . The smell immediately dissipated.  Sometimes   it's good to be a mage . Darius turned  to regard  the  small  man coolly; he knew  he  was staring at the deep red dragon brand on his cheek, the mark that identified him. "You are a mage," the bald man said, though it sounded more a question than a statement .   Darius nodded. "Yet you are of the Church, despite what the priests of Aurtus have done to your people. ”  The statement again was more of a question.  Darius nodded a second time; it had not been the first time someone had stared unbelievingly at the mage who served under men whose ancestors had  repeatedly  tried to exterminate his people. The Agreement had changed all of that .  Iseni, so strong and sure ,  had led her people to a stalemate with the  K ingdom  of  Mundanes ,  and the Church, forcing them to capitulate and allow mages to become full citizens for the first time in ages.  Darius was quiet a moment and then nodded at the man.   "I am a mage, but more importantly, I am a speaker .  I serve Aurtus, not the priests or the king; however, to be a speaker, one must have the power to manipulate their surroundings, one must be a mage and a priest."  The man stood there confused, his eyes staring into nowhere as he processed  the   words.   Finally, his gaze returned to Darius, and he nodded with a smile. "Alright, your holy spellcaster, let's see what the young prince can tell us; they wouldn't let me examine the body until you had arrived . "  T he little man  chuckled at his joke as he turned away, but then stopped short and turned back with awkward contrition of a dog who had stolen food from the hearth . "I apologize, Lord Speaker .  I am Murat .  I am the one who takes care of those passed .   S ometimes my decorum is quite rusty ;  please forgive the joke . "  Without waiting for a response, he motioned to the Lord Speaker to follow  him to the table that bore the prince. "Murat, are you a doctor by chance?" Darius asked, not daring to hope .   A  doctor could be invaluable this evening in helping to identify what had happened to this man .   Murat shook his head .  " M ore like an undertaker, my  l ord.   I take the bodies and ensure that the relatives can stomach to look at them, then I display them for the proper 12 days so that everyone can say goodbye to the deceased . " Murat waddled past Darius ,  giving the Lord Speaker a slight bow as he made his way to the  table .  With practiced motions , he pulled the sheet off to reveal the bloated ,   twisted   body of the young prince. Despite the yellowing corpse being well past rigor, his face still held the ghastly scream that had signaled the young man's demise; dried blood spread across the   grote s que   maw that had been his mouth ,   lending  to the  king 's tale of blood. "Who has been here to see the body?" Darius asked with detached professionalism .   W hen the man didn't answer ,  Darius looked up curiously, noticing the small man was transfixed by the prince's face , frozen   in  a macabre death scream. He couldn't blame the man. Though he had probably seen just as many dead bodies as the  speaker  himself, the look of fear and pain on the greying face was enough to make even the most hardened man pause. Snapping his fingers,  and  Murat  jumped to  attention. "I'm sorry, Speaker,"  he   stammered, "just … the pain he must have felt … " "How many have come to view the body?" Darius repeated. This time the pause from Murat was cerebral. With a nod and a confident tone, he said, "Seven, Speaker." Not many,  he thought, knowing at least three of them would have been the  king , the old woman, and the head of security. The others were not that important.   The killer most likely would not have scheduled time with the body . Circling the table, he studied the dead prince ,  allowing the details to wash over his mind, opening his perception, controlling his breathing . P utting the training of the Keep  to use ,  no area of the young prince went overlooked. "No signs of bruising or scratching .   M inimal signs of a struggle, except for…"  Darius leaned closer to s tudy the contours of the prince's face .   The jaw was tight ,  and the brow deeply furrowed. This man had seen death coming and knew what had killed him.  He realized that whatever the cause of his demise, it  had been   engineered to cause maximum pain for the victim. After a few contemplative moments, he turned to Murat .  " Y ou might want to step back . "  T he undertaker  gave   him a curious look  and  took a few steps towards the door, his  focus  on th e   s peaker ’ s work . Blowing out a breath, the  speaker 's eyes  searched   the body as he continued to collect clues. Darius carefully rolled up his sleeve,  revealing as  ornate leather wraps.   The  j eweled leather band, thick with markings burned deep into its surface, was strangely beautiful.   C oming  from  the bracelet were delicate leather tassels, intertwined in a patterned weave and covering the entire forearm, each  one   carefully engraved with crystal runic script. Murat stepped  closer,  fear being replaced with curiosity as he studied each tassel .   T he incredibly detailed script was breathtaking.   "What is that ? " the large man whispered .   Darius smiled flatly. "It is something only a speaker can use, my friend . "  C losing his eyes,  he  breath ed  the words ,  "Videre  v erum corpus," pushing his will into the phrase as he felt the  bracer  heat. The  runic letters on the tassels began to pulse a glowing green color. Darius's eyes remained closed, repeating the strange words over and over ,  his face set in a determined mask. The more he repeated the words, the more the letters began to glow, no longer pulsing but now a steady green, the glow now increasing with every repetition of the phrase.  Darius  swept   his arm over the body, and a green smoke began to emanate from the woven leather band. Falling over the body, it began to cover the dead prince. Repeating the words, Darius pushed more of his will into the magic as the smoke enveloped the entire corpse. Once it was covered, Darius pulled the arm away, his cloak covering the band as the green glow began to dissipate. As both men watched, the smoke rose from the body, forming a perfect simulacrum of the prince ,  float ing  four feet  above   the table. Leaning in, Darius studied the smoke. "Notice my friend, there are no entry wounds, no weapons used on the prince .   W hatever killed him was not physical . "  W ith a wave of his hand, the smokey replica rotated, allowing Darius to see every angle of spectral simulation.   Suddenly Darius held his hand, and the simulacrum stopped . A  section of the replicant's smoky arm pulsed with white light. "What is this?" Darius whispered,  spreading   his fingers, and the smoke  grew , making the floating representation grow to double in size. "Look at this, my friend .   I t appears to be something burned into the prince's hand and arm," Darius whispered and motioned Murat forward. The large man shuffled slowly as if scared of the thing floating above the table. "What is it? What does it say?" he whispered, looking between Darius and the floating visual. "It's a word, though I am not familiar with it," he said, though not to anyone in particular, and with a final wave of his hand, the smoky apparition dissolved before them . " D razaho ," Murat whispered ,  trying to discern letters burnt into the flesh  as if the word itself were a weapon he was afraid  assault him.   "It is not a word I am familiar with, nor is it one that I have seen used by mages .   H owever, with what the investigators for the  king  have been studying …t hey seem to be leaning in that direction ,  and that ,  my friend ,  could be very, very dangerous . "It appears I have my work cut out for me .”  Darius turned and headed back for the door , r eturning to his escort .   H e nodded at the old man. "Take me to where the prince spent most of his time .” *** The aged soldier opened a door and stepped aside for Darius to pass. Now i n the castle's attic,  he found himself in  an old dusty wooden chamber filled with ancient relics ,  carefully laid upon shelves  that lined   the old room's wall s . In the center stood three tables placed around a large firepit; the pit looked blackened and well - used .   W here once a raging fire would heat the room, it now stood silent and dark. The old man busied himself, lighting the candles and sconces dott ing  the large room. As he did, areas of the old chamber began to illuminate, highlighting the items and relics clearly.   Walking amongst the tables and shelves,  Darius   looked over the odd items laid out as if in a museum display. Darius gently picked up a strange - looking knife ,  running his fingers over the sleek hilt .   H e appreciated the feel of the odd material, soft yet firm. The blade's base held more peculiar lettering, this one reading 'Ontario .’   S tudying the black edge, Darius moved it back and forth, allowing the light to catch the odd ,  thin ,  obsidian paint  coating   the metal.   He had never seen its equal — not even in the high-quality mage weapons he had seen forged within the Order .   P utting the knife back, he looked along the other interesting relics before turning back to the old soldier.   "Where are we?" "You asked me to take you to where the prince spent most of his time. ”  Darius toured the room .   This was  the prince’s  passion .   H e collected relics of the ancient world, of the first ones .   S ince the only ones that existed landed when man returned to earth, the se  were rare  treasures .   The old man cleared his throat and  point ed  to the closest table .  " H e was lying there .   S ome of the relics had fallen around him .   H e had been dead only a short time .   He was alone . H owever, there is suspicion over who might have done it . "  He  looked  pointedly  at Darius.  Mages , he thought to himself, turning his back to the old man, not wanting to show the anger that flashed across his face.   Darius instead took to studying the tables, looking over the handwritten notebooks . Some  artifacts   he could guess at their use, and others were a complete mystery .   He picked   up another item, one side covered in a dark glass that had shattered long ago .   B arely visible on the reverse side was white lettering he did not recognize , but he sounded it out as best he could.  "Samsung," he whispered ,  and with a shrug, gently replaced the item on the display shelf. Darius could imagine this was a place of solace for the young prince, for one who se  every moment   in  life  was planned, who se every movement  was critiqued .   T his was a place he could get away and be himself. "Who was in charge of his security that night? I will need to speak with him," Darius commanded, and the old man nodded  and left the room , leaving the  speaker  alone in the cavernous warehouse of  oddities . It didn't take long before the old man returned with a rather unpleasant - looking squat soldier in the shiniest armor that Darius had ever seen.  He  could see the slight grey in the close-cropped black hair, the shadow of battle scars on his neck and arms'. This was not someone who had spent his career sitting behind a guard post, but then someone who would be the key guard of an important person such as the prince wouldn't be, he mused, waiting for the  c aptain to speak.  The guard marched over to Darius and ,  clicking his heels, stood at rigid attention before announcing himself.  “ Guard Captain Heathrow reporting, sir, ”  the man barked, causing Darius to wince at the volume.  "Well  m et ,  Soldier," Darius said . The soldier bristled.  "It's  C aptain, sir," he corrected, the 'sir' coming out less like a sign of respect and more like a slur . "Forgive me, Captain,"  Darius   said   as he watched the  c aptain's eyes focused on the tattoo on his right cheek .   This man doesn't trust me . And he doesn’t like mages. "Captain, what can you tell me about the night the prince passed ? " he asked and then, as if an afterthought, looked at him and waved his hand .   “ Stand at ease . " It was plain  as  the man  shifted into a slightly more relaxed stance that he  did not like being there, and more importantly, he was not pleased about being summoned by a mage. "Sir, as was his custom most nights, the prince had retired to work on his antiquities and requested to be alone. I had two guards stationed at the doorway and another at the base of the stairs, as always.   I had signed off for the evening . H owever, I can make  them  available to you should you need it. ” A good soldier , Darius thought. "Sir, ” the man’s terse tone spoke to his displeasure for being commanded by a mage,   “ I was awakened shortly before dawn by one of my guards and rushed here as soon as I was notified .   I t was no more than mere minutes between being notified and my arriving . " A shadow passed over the man's face as he recalled what  Darius thought  was probably the biggest failure of his career .  "Once I arrived,  I found  the prince's body lying at the foot of the table .  I was informed he had been heating some of the relics ,  as he often did to see how they reacted,  as  part of his research. “ I checked the body .  I noticed the runic word burnt into his hand and arm .   T he body had bled out .   I t looked as if he had expelled it from his mouth .   N o one had been with the prince, according to the guards … no one they could see ,  that is . "  Darius  pondered   the way the man ha d  said that last statement .   T his man suspect s  a mage had found a way up here without the guards seeing them .  And h e  thinks he  knows who ,  Darius realized with surprise .   W hy do I get the feeling they already have a suspect, and my investigation is simply to confirm that ?   Staying quiet, the  speaker  continued to wander around the room, giving a moment of calm as he formulated his next words.   "Captain, from the sound of your words, it seems you feel this death was caused by magic," he stated .  "Or a mage."  "Sir," the  c aptain quickly  affirmed , and the venom in the word  lingering  long after the acoustics of the attic had allowed the resonance to go silent. The quiet hung in the room as the  speaker  turned, and the two men stood, staring at each other.  Finally, despite the myriad of questions he wanted  t o  ask , Darius  thanked the captain and waved him off dismissively. The  c aptain  b ristled, but true to his position, he came to attention, saluted the  speaker , spun deftly on his heels, and marched out, the old soldier watching him go.
